outcome: Fetal acidaemia (umbilical artery cord pH < 7.20 at birth)
cohort: 294 women with term singleton pregnancies complicated by an umbilical artery cord pH < 7.20 at birth, matched with 294 controls with umbilical artery cord pH > 7.20
finding: Pregestational diabetes and urinary tract infection were associated with an increased risk of fetal acidaemia, while low maternal BMI, pyrexia in labor, electronic fetal monitoring, and emergency cesarean section were found to be protective.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section was found to be protective against fetal acidaemia (OR 0.42; 95% CI 0.26-0.66; P < 0.001).
